Proposal for the first brain (short, principles only): 1) Keep pieces coordinated; develop before grabbing material. 2) King safety first: castle early, avoid pawn storms on our own king. 3) Never hang material; check every opponent capture and check before moving. 4) Captain and advisor should both verify the opponent's last move and any tactic (forks, pins, back-rank) before each move. 5) Prefer simple, sound plans: central control, open files for rooks, trade when ahead. 6) If the position is lost, play on for tricks; resign only when clearly lost.

2) Castle early; keep our own king safe from pawn storms.

7) Resign only when clearly lost.
8) Learn from each game: note the opponent's habits and our own blunders.

A02: A02: Played 18.Rxe5 (I'm captain). The rook is defended by d4, so Qxe5 dxe5 wins Black's queen. d4 is covered by Bc3 and Qd1. Next for A01: Re1 to e-file pressure (Rfe8 is the likely reply), trade rooks, then Qe2/Qf3 with Bb4 or Ba5 ideas on the queen.
A02: A02: Played 20.Qd3 (I'm captain). Ra1 covers the first rank, so Re1+ Rxe1. Qe2/Qe1 hang the queen to Re8. Next for A01: consider Rf1 or Re1 to trade rooks, keep d4 defended, and use the extra pawn (we have 7 v 5). Watch Re2 and Qxd4 tricks.

A02: A02: Black's Qe6 eyes a2 (diagonal e6-d5-c4-b3-a2). Suggest 23.d5: a pawn fork-tempo on the queen (d5 attacks e6), and it opens the Bc3 diagonal toward g7.
